findings.claim: Camera cache reuse permits historical receipts without settings-bound identity, so it does not enforce the advertised exact request/settings/binding/schema reuse contract.
findings.evidence: The function explicitly enables reuse for role='camera', stage='camera-direction' at line 20. At line 47, cacheIdentity and baseRequestHash are checked only when present. The subsequently reconstructed provider requestHash binds routing to provider, model and base_url, not the complete model settings. Consequently, the historical-receipt branch can authorize camera reuse without proving that generation settings match the current configuration. The reuse report expressly labels this branch 'historical-accepted-contract-revalidated' and generationSettingsHistoricallyBound=false. Current domain revalidation does not supply the missing historical settings proof. This conflicts with cameraDirectionDescription.reuse, which requires exact settings.
findings.suggestedSourceChange: For camera-direction reuse, require both receipt.cacheIdentity === receiptIdentity and receipt.baseRequestHash === hash(receiptBaseRequest), rejecting receipts that omit either field. Keep the successful journal/model-artifact proof and current domain revalidation requirements unchanged. Historical compatibility for other planning stages need not be changed.

scopeLimitations: Reviewed only the four supplied complete TypeScript files and the exact bounded excerpts and prompt text in docs/topics/reviews/camera-source-review-context-v1.md. Supplied digest strings were not independently verified.

The implementation of planWithValidation and its receipt-writing, retry and budget behavior was not supplied. The creative storyboard checkpoint is visibly written before camera planning, and a validated cache hit calls camera planning outside the director-cache validation catch; complete budget-failure resume behavior remains unreviewed.

CameraSchema, canonical storyboard schemas, hashing utilities, model routing, provider adapters and journal writers were not supplied. Their internal validation, request identity and proof semantics remain unreviewed.

The supplied camera callback invokes the existing full creative normalizer and then checks camera-only preservation. The internals of imported source, actor, contact, world-clock, camera, scene-security and artwork validators were not supplied and are unreviewed.

The bounded configuration excerpt shows omitted/null camera settings inheriting a clone of storyboard settings. Full settings-update persistence, inherited routing after later director changes, and actual router behavior were not supplied and remain unreviewed.
No execution, tests, tools, runtime acceptance, imagery, voice, cinematography or video quality were evaluated. All source, actor, artwork, voice, contact and final-production gates remain unchanged.
